title: 10-Year Treasury Yield

source.name: FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)

summary: The 10-Year Treasury Yield closed at 4.35% on 2026-04-27, up 4 basis points from 4.31% on 2026-04-24. The yield has ranged between 4.30% and 4.35% over the past week, showing modest upward movement.
key_points: Source: FRED series DGS10, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
why_it_matters: The 10-year Treasury yield is a foundational benchmark that influences mortgage rates, corporate borrowing costs, and equity valuations. At 4.35%, it reflects current market pricing of the risk-free rate and expectations for the path of monetary policy. Rising yields generally pressure risk assets and increase financing costs across the economy. [Note: Context added from general macro knowledge, not from source.]
macro_context: The yield level reflects market expectations for Fed policy, inflation, and economic growth. A yield at 4.35% suggests the market is pricing a relatively elevated rate environment for the medium term. [Note: Context added from general macro knowledge, not from source.]
